drafted_from: tool:github:ggml-org-whisper.cpp's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs whisper.cpp.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use whisper.cpp on my computer to transcribe speech in an audio or video file to text on your own computer: the file is interview.wav." It reads the row, installs whisper.cpp if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: whisper.cpp is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use whisper.cpp on interview.wav". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:ggml-org-whisper.cpp"}.

2. It checks that git, cmake, a C++ compiler are on your computer, and if whisper.cpp is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp.git ; cd whisper.cpp ; sh ./models/download-ggml-model.sh base.en ; cmake -B build ; cmake --build build -j --config Release.
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input}: ./build/bin/whisper-cli -m models/ggml-base.en.bin -f interview.wav
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: whisper.cpp on a 30 second interview recording of Sam, a baker, talking about her shop
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:ggml-org-whisper.cpp runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got whisper.cpp in, the command line: ./build/bin/whisper-cli -m models/ggml-base.en.bin -f interview.wav  (synthetic input: a 30 second interview recording of Sam, a baker, talking about her shop).
worked_examples.hands_back: Each line whisper-cli prints is a time range and the words spoken in it, for example "[00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:06.000]   Hi, I am Sam and I run a small bakery." The transcript is on screen only; nothing is written to a file.
